deals.date_text: 2021 (club estimate reported in November 2021; LaLiga Impulso signed December 2021)
deals.headline: Villarreal to receive about EUR 108m from LaLiga's CVC deal
deals.summary: Under LaLiga Impulso, CVC funded LaLiga's clubs in exchange for 10.95% of the net revenue LaLiga manages. Villarreal's share came as participative loans from the league, repayable over 50 years (to 2072) with 1.52% of its TV income; EUR 108,599,966.90 was outstanding at 30 June 2025 (club accounts, note 9). The club used it to rebuild the Estadio de la Cerámica. CVC holds no stake in the club itself.

deals.headline: Villarreal spends about EUR 70m rebuilding the municipal Estadio de la Cerámica
deals.investor: Villarreal C.F., S.A.D. (funded with its LaLiga Impulso participative loan)
deals.summary: The club paid for the rebuild of the municipally owned stadium (new corner stand, full roof, façade, seating and screens), finished in 2023. Its accounts say the work is financed with the participative loan signed with LaLiga.

name: Villarreal C.F., S.A.D.
notes: Revenue, staff costs, operating and pre-tax results come from the club's audited 2024-25 accounts, a scanned PDF with no text layer, so each evidence string is the figure exactly as printed in the income statement (net turnover EUR 95,437,900.05, down from EUR 119,721,562.42). The year's EUR 13.7m net profit came mainly from EUR 94.7m of gains on player sales. The net profit (EUR 13,711,248.56) is also in the club's AGM release, and the 2025-26 budget is EUR 215.2m. Nomar Patrimonial's 98.79% is likewise read from the scanned accounts (note 9.d); Economía Digital confirms Nomar is Roig's holding that owns the club. Demócrata (August 2026) says the Cerámica belongs to Villarreal, but the club's own accounts and Relevo say the Ajuntament de Vila-real owns it. No valuation, net-debt figure, social-media counts or league titles (none won) were recorded; the 2024-25 attendance is a press figure based on 2Playbook data.

ownership_summary: Villarreal C.F., S.A.D. is controlled by Fernando Roig Alfonso, president since the 1997-98 season, through Nomar Patrimonial, S.L.U. (Almazora, Castellón), the holding company that also owns his Pamesa ceramics group. The club's audited accounts say Nomar held 98.79% of the share capital at 30 June 2025, and Nomar heads the group the club belongs to. Fernando Roig Negueroles is managing director (consejero delegado).
